title: Heading and subheading markers
rationale: Removes one or more leading hash markers while preserving the heading words.
originalText:
# Installation

## First run

Select a short sentence and press the global hotkey.
expectedPreparedText:
Installation

First run

Select a short sentence and press the global hotkey.

title: Unordered list marker styles
rationale: Removes dash, asterisk, plus, and bullet markers without changing the list content.
originalText:
- Keep the original voice.
* Restore the clipboard.
+ Preserve normal hotkeys.
• Stop playback immediately.
expectedPreparedText:
Keep the original voice.
Restore the clipboard.
Preserve normal hotkeys.
Stop playback immediately.

title: URL path and query punctuation
rationale: Makes the scheme colon, path dash, and query separators audible only inside a detected URL.
expectedPreparedText: Open https colon example.com/pulse dash reader/docs question mark voice equals heart and speed equals 1 for the current instructions.

title: Bare filename punctuation
rationale: Expands the dash and known extension dot in a filename without touching decimal numbers.
originalText: Inspect review-notes.txt and PulseReader.exe before continuing.
expectedPreparedText: Inspect review dash notes dot txt and PulseReader dot exe before continuing.

title: Timestamp with seconds
rationale: Preserves every digit group in a full timestamp, including leading zeroes.
expectedPreparedText: twelve oh four oh nine Starting synthesis. nine oh five oh one Playback completed.

title: Controlled table cell and row pauses
rationale: Keeps each row in one utterance and uses semicolons for a lighter pause between cells.
originalText:
Voice | Speed | Volume
Heart | 1.0 | 100
George | 0.95 | 90
Sarah | 1.10 | 80
expectedPreparedText:
Voice; Speed; Volume.
Heart; 1.0; 100.
George; 0.95; 90.
Sarah; 1.10; 80.

title: Command, filename, and dotted setting
rationale: Applies a small technical vocabulary and reads dots only inside recognised identifiers.
originalText: Run dotnet build, inspect PulseReader.exe, and set speech.backend=kokoro. Keep net10.0 unchanged.
expectedPreparedText: Run dot net build, inspect PulseReader dot exe, and set speech dot backend equals kokoro. Keep net10.0 unchanged.

title: Dotted time before p.m.
rationale: Treats a dotted value as a time only when an a.m. or p.m. suffix removes the ambiguity.
originalText: The meeting starts at 3.30 p.m. and ends at 4.05 p.m.
expectedPreparedText: The meeting starts at three thirty p.m. and ends at four oh five p.m.

title: Typographic apostrophes inside contractions
rationale: Normalises curly apostrophes between letters so contractions remain one word.
originalText: I’ve checked it. It can’t stall, it doesn’t crash, and it isn’t noisy.
expectedPreparedText: I've checked it. It can't stall, it doesn't crash, and it isn't noisy.

title: A slash B abbreviation
rationale: Adds a full stop after A so Kokoro pronounces it as a standalone letter while retaining the slash.
originalText: Run an A/B comparison before approval.
expectedPreparedText: Run an A./B comparison before approval.

title: Literal time-format token
rationale: Spaces the existing colons so Kokoro separates the three format groups without inserting spoken punctuation words.
expectedPreparedText: The parser accepts HH : MM : SS timestamps.

title: Standalone A before the word slash
rationale: Treats A as a letter when it introduces an explicit A slash B comparison.

title: Standalone A referenced inside a sentence
rationale: Treats an internal capital A as a referenced letter rather than a lowercase article.
originalText: Adds a full stop after A so Kokoro pronounces it as a standalone letter.
expectedPreparedText: Adds a full stop after A. so Kokoro pronounces it as a standalone letter.

title: Standalone A in a variant label
rationale: Treats A as a letter when label punctuation follows it.

title: Standalone A used as an option name
rationale: Treats an internal capital A as the name of an option.
originalText: Option A is selected, while option B remains available.
expectedPreparedText: Option A. is selected, while option B remains available.

title: Ordinary sentence-opening article
rationale: Leaves a sentence-opening A alone when it functions as the article a.
originalText: A good reading should sound natural.
expectedPreparedText: A good reading should sound natural.

title: Ordinary article at the start of a heading
rationale: Removes the Markdown marker but leaves the heading's opening article as A.
